items.title: SSRF policy has no locked enforcement algorithm
items.statement: The registry stores an SSRF/private-host policy and webfetch validates URL syntax and scheme, but this window never requires address resolution checks, redirect-hop revalidation, DNS-rebinding resistance, or consistent enforcement across provider-native and PM fallback paths.
items.impact: A syntactically valid public URL can resolve or redirect to loopback, link-local, private, or metadata endpoints, with provider fallback creating inconsistent egress behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Lock the address classes, resolution timing, redirect policy, and fail-closed behavior at the dispatcher boundary for every execution path.

evidence.exact_quote: - The WebProviderAdapterRegistry is the PM-owned single source of truth for web provider and adapter capability. Registry rows bind provider ID, adapter ID, adapter kind (`pm_native`, `direct_api`, `mcp_server`, `model_native`, `cli_bridge`, or `server_bridge`), operation capability, support tier, effective cost/cache policy, fallback rank, health state, robots behavior, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential reference, and projection state. Provider config files, MCP projections, model-native provider projections, coding-agent projections, and GUI settings rows are consumers of this registry, not competing sources of provider truth, and they must serialize credential references only, never raw secrets.

- webfetch URL handling is locked: reject non-HTTP(S) schemes such as `file://`, `ftp://`, and `javascript:`, normalize before routing, default bare domains to https://, reject malformed URLs with invalid_input, and enforce a default 5 MB max_content_length unless configured otherwise.

items.title: Wildcard research approval silently authorizes discovered hosts
items.statement: Search and research receive wildcard-only approval even though autonomous and composed research automatically read discovered URLs; the contract does not define whether host-scoped approval is re-entered before reads, how redirects and embedded origins are surfaced, or how users constrain discovery egress.
items.impact: One broad approval can fan out to sensitive, unexpected, costly, or policy-forbidden sites without a visible authority transition.
items.builder_discretion: Define the permission transition from discovery to each read and the visible host/fan-out bound.

evidence.exact_quote: - When `autonomous: true` is set on `webresearch`, PM may use provider-native autonomous research when available; Firecrawl delegates to `/v2/agent`, Tavily uses its advanced search + extract chain, and other providers use the PM-composed enhanced recipe: search, read top pages through Site Reader, refine and repeat only when evidence is insufficient, then synthesize with citations. Autonomous research remains bounded to at most three search iterations, at most `max_sources` page reads, and a 120s total runtime unless a narrower provider or run limit applies; each step surfaces activity such as `Searching Web: <refined query>` and `Reading Site: <url>`.

- Permission requests for `websearch` and `webresearch` are wildcard-only operation approvals because the URL set is not known before discovery, while `/extract/crawl/map` and `webfetch` use host/site-scoped approvals when their target is known.

items.title: Prompt-injection visibility is not an enforcement boundary
items.statement: PageRepresentation exposes prompt-injection chips and audit fields, but no normative rule says how untrusted page instructions are isolated from agent instructions, when actions are blocked, or what downstream consumers must do with the indicator.
items.impact: A malicious page can influence synthesis or browser actions while the system remains technically compliant by merely displaying a chip.
items.builder_discretion: Define taint propagation, instruction separation, action gating, and auditable override behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: The Site Reader renderer pipeline MUST build a structured `PageRepresentation` rather than returning an untyped page dump. It extracts the accessibility tree, layout bounds for relevant nodes, landmarks, headings, interactive elements, forms, content summary/full content according to the requested detail level, and optionally discovered/merged iframe content. The representation carries typed page structure, interactive elements, forms, errors, optional interactive summary, optional iframes, console/network refs, screenshot/PDF artifact refs when requested, redaction profile IDs, and visible prompt-injection chips so downstream agents can reason about the page before acting. Prompt-injection indicators are visible chips and audit fields, not hidden prompt text.

items.title: Binary safety trusts server-declared Content-Type
items.statement: Binary handling is keyed only from HTTP Content-Type and allows SVG as an inline attachment, but does not require MIME sniffing, decompression limits, content-disposition handling, active-content sanitization, or streaming enforcement when content-length is absent or false.
items.impact: Mislabelled, compressed, polyglot, or active content can bypass conversion and size assumptions or execute in an unsafe attachment viewer.
items.builder_discretion: Specify byte-level type checks, streaming caps, decompression budgets, SVG treatment, and safe attachment rendering.

evidence.exact_quote: - Binary `/non-text` webfetch URL responses are detected from the HTTP `Content-Type` header. Supported image types (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/svg+xml`; source shorthands `/png`, `/jpeg`, `/gif`, `/webp`, and `/svg`) return as inline attachments with MIME type preserved and size capped by `max_content_length` (5 MB by default). Unsupported or `/large` binary media such as video, audio, or executables returns metadata only (`MIME type`, `content-length`, `URL`) without downloading the body, and non-text responses do not enter HTML-to-Markdown conversion.

items.title: Default cache storage lacks privacy partition and lifecycle rules
items.statement: Read, extract, crawl, and map content is stored by default, while the window does not bind cache entries to project/user/credential/permission context or define encryption, redaction-before-store, deletion, retention, logout, or credential-revocation behavior.
items.impact: Authenticated or sensitive page content can be replayed across authority contexts or retained beyond the user's intent.
items.builder_discretion: Lock cache partition keys, redaction order, retention and purge triggers, and credential/permission invalidation semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: - Operation cache TTL defaults are exact unless overridden by caller policy: `websearch` defaults `cache_policy?: { max_age_seconds?: number, store?: boolean }` to `{ max_age_seconds: 3600, store: true }`; `webfetch` and `webextract` default the same shape to `{max_age_seconds: 14400, store: true}`; `webcrawl` and `webmap` default the same shape to `{ max_age_seconds: 86400, store: true }`. `webresearch` may reuse cached search/read/extract artifacts under those operation TTLs, but the synthesized research answer is task-specific and is not cached as reusable web content. Non-fetch web operations that use the shared web cache expose `cache_policy` input and `cache_state` output rather than relying on invisible TTL-only caching.

items.title: Change tracking has no atomic crawl generation model
items.statement: Per-page status compares against a previous crawl but does not identify the committed baseline, define concurrent crawl serialization, or prevent an interrupted crawl from becoming the next baseline.
items.impact: Overlapping or failed crawls can report false changed/removed states and corrupt subsequent change summaries.
items.builder_discretion: Use immutable crawl generation IDs and atomically promote only a completed baseline, with explicit incomplete status.

evidence.exact_quote: - For `webcrawl` change tracking, each crawled page is compared to the previous crawl of the same root URL and the output includes a per-page `change_status` field with `new`, `same`, `changed`, or `removed`; removed pages are pages present in the previous crawl but absent from the current crawl, and `change_summary` reports counts for each status.

items.title: Sequential actions lack partial-execution and timeout recovery semantics
items.statement: The contract locks per-action and total timeouts and sequential order but never defines cancellation, which prior actions remain committed, how the failing index is returned, session cleanup, retry safety, or resumability.
items.impact: A timeout after form entry, navigation, or clicks leaves unknown side effects and invites unsafe replay of the full action array.
items.builder_discretion: Return a per-action outcome ledger and terminal state, define cancellation/cleanup, and make retry eligibility explicit.

evidence.exact_quote: - `WebAction.timeout_ms` / `timeout_ms` defaults to 5000ms; max 30000ms; total across all actions capped at 30s
- Actions are executed sequentially in array order

items.title: The exact WebAction enum conflicts with guaranteed browser action IDs
items.statement: The declared type union omits guaranteed IDs such as open_tab, hover, drag, upload_file, handle_dialog, and verification actions, while no discriminator or conversion contract separates the research WebAction type from the broader browser-testing action type.
items.impact: Callers, persistence, permissions, and adapters can disagree on which actions are valid and normalize the same request differently.
items.builder_discretion: Name distinct types or publish one superset plus profile restrictions and canonical serialization rules.

evidence.exact_quote: - Guaranteed everyday browser/testing action IDs include `open_tab`, `select_tab`, `close_tab`, `click`, `type`, `fill_form`, `select_option`, `hover`, `drag`, `press_key`, `upload_file`, `handle_dialog`, `wait_for`, `verify_text`, `verify_element`, `verify_value`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `console`, `network`, and `set_viewport`; advanced `/testing` actions include `trace_start`, `trace_stop`, `video_start`, `video_stop`, `export_pdf`, `cookie_*`, `local_storage_*`, `session_storage_*`, `network_offline`, `network_online`, `route_mock`, and `generate_locator`.
- `type: "click" | "scroll" | "type" | "press_key" | "wait_for" | "navigate" | "screenshot" | "set_viewport" | "fill_form" | "select_option" | "back" | "reload" | "snapshot" | "console" | "network";`

items.title: Unsupported input has three incompatible outcomes
items.statement: One rule maps unsupported input to invalid_input, another requires unsupported_operation for a source/category, and unavailable requested formats become only a warning. The window has no precedence table separating malformed input, unsupported operation, unavailable runtime, and partial success.
items.impact: Adapters and GUI consumers can render the same condition as user error, hard failure, or successful degradation, making tests and remediation unreliable.
items.builder_discretion: Define mutually exclusive predicates and precedence for each canonical error/warning and resulting success value.

evidence.exact_quote: - The web dispatcher maps each invocation to one canonical operation (`search`, `extract`, `research`, `deep_research`, `crawl`, `map`, or `fetch`/`read`), validates parameters against that operation's contract before adapter routing, and rejects malformed or unsupported inputs with `invalid_input` instead of handing them to a provider.

- Multiple extraction `formats` may be requested together. `screenshot` and `pdf` formats require browser runtime; when that runtime is unavailable, return a `capability_unavailable` warning rather than an error. `export_pdf` is retired as a browser/trace action for research access; callers request PDF capture through `webfetch` with `formats: ["pdf"]`. Trace/video actions are testing evidence only and are excluded from `research_session` web-operation actions.

items.title: JSON Schema processing is size-capped but not complexity- or fetch-capped
items.statement: The schema limit is 50KB and $ref is supported, but the contract does not forbid remote references or bound reference depth, recursion, branch expansion, validation time, output size, or regex complexity.
items.impact: A small hostile schema can trigger remote fetches, exponential validation, recursion, excessive output, or dispatcher starvation.
items.builder_discretion: Require local-only references and explicit depth, node, time, output, and pattern-complexity budgets.

evidence.exact_quote: - `schema_too_large` means the extraction schema exceeds the 50KB limit. `schema_invalid` means the schema is not valid JSON Schema draft-07.

- Schema-backed web extraction uses JSON Schema draft-07. Supported schema constructs include `$ref`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `enum`, `required`, and nested objects/arrays; providers may narrow unsupported constructs only with structured `schema_invalid` or `schema_too_large` feedback rather than silently flattening the schema.

items.title: Iframe extraction has no origin permission inheritance or total budget
items.statement: Iframe traversal is depth-limited, but the contract does not specify whether newly discovered frame origins require approval, how cookies/storage are partitioned, or a cap on frame count, bytes, time, and diagnostic sessions.
items.impact: One approved parent can cause unbounded cross-origin evidence collection, privacy leakage, or a frame-fanout denial of service.
items.builder_discretion: Define origin inheritance and explicit per-page frame/session/byte/time budgets with fail-closed attribution.

evidence.exact_quote: Site Reader iframe handling is read-target behavior, not inline visualizer sandboxing. During structured reading, PM recursively discovers nested iframes up to 3 levels deep, attempts cross-origin iframe content extraction only where browser security policy allows, gracefully skips blocked same-origin or X-Frame-Options cases with a warning, may use per-frame diagnostic sessions when the PM-managed native browser runtime is available, and merges iframe content into the parent `PageRepresentation` with source-frame attribution. Playwright and CDP are reference/fallback test-driver vocabulary only; they do not replace the PM-managed native browser runtime or become product terms.

items.title: Requested-format degradation has no partial-success truth model
items.statement: A missing browser runtime only emits a warning for screenshot/PDF, while the common envelope has one success boolean and no required per-format outcome. The GUI can therefore show success even though a specifically requested artifact is absent.
items.impact: Users and downstream consumers can treat an incomplete result as complete or retry the wrong subsystem.
items.builder_discretion: Require requested-versus-returned format outcomes and define success semantics when any required format is missing.

evidence.exact_quote: - Multiple extraction `formats` may be requested together. `screenshot` and `pdf` formats require browser runtime; when that runtime is unavailable, return a `capability_unavailable` warning rather than an error. `export_pdf` is retired as a browser/trace action for research access; callers request PDF capture through `webfetch` with `formats: ["pdf"]`. Trace/video actions are testing evidence only and are excluded from `research_session` web-operation actions.

- Web operation outputs share a locked common result envelope: `success: boolean`, `web_operation`, `support_tier`, `execution_path`, `requested_adapter_id?`, `effective_adapter_id?`, `adapter_selection_reason?`, `projection_freshness?`, `projection_health?`, `provider_fallback_occurred: boolean`, `provider_fallback_summary?`, `source_count?: number`, `sources?: Array<{ title?, url, snippet?, provenance_badge? }>`, `warnings?: string[]`, `error_code?: string`, and `error_message?: string`.

items.title: Highest-priority provider selection is not deterministic enough to test
items.statement: The registry exposes fallback rank, health, cost/cache policy, and projection state, but the deterministic recipe only says highest-priority provider. Tie-breaking, stale projection behavior, health transitions, cost ceilings, and fallback eligibility are not ordered.
items.impact: Identical requests can route differently across implementations or time, defeating reproducibility and surprising users with cost or capability changes.
items.builder_discretion: Publish a total ordering and snapshot the evaluated registry version and reasons per invocation.

evidence.exact_quote: - The WebProviderAdapterRegistry is the PM-owned single source of truth for web provider and adapter capability. Registry rows bind provider ID, adapter ID, adapter kind (`pm_native`, `direct_api`, `mcp_server`, `model_native`, `cli_bridge`, or `server_bridge`), operation capability, support tier, effective cost/cache policy, fallback rank, health state, robots behavior, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential reference, and projection state. Provider config files, MCP projections, model-native provider projections, coding-agent projections, and GUI settings rows are consumers of this registry, not competing sources of provider truth, and they must serialize credential references only, never raw secrets.

- When `autonomous: false` or omitted on `webresearch`, the default PM-composed research recipe is deterministic and bounded: search with the highest-priority provider, select top candidate URLs up to `max_sources`, read/extract up to `auto_read_cap` pages via Site Reader as the auto-read cap, then synthesize an answer with citations from read content. In this branch the agent does NOT navigate or interact with pages; interaction-capable browser work must route through the explicit WebAction or browser/session contracts.

items.title: LSP rename approval does not define safe apply or rollback
items.statement: Rename requires approval, but this window does not require previewing the complete WorkspaceEdit, checking document versions, validating paths and permissions, handling overlapping edits, applying atomically, or rolling back a partial write.
items.impact: An approved rename can corrupt multiple files or apply stale edits with no deterministic recovery.
items.builder_discretion: Lock preview evidence, version preconditions, atomic application, journaled rollback, and partial-failure reporting.

evidence.exact_quote: - `rename` with explicit approval before apply

items.title: Muted chat messages may still be returned to the agent
items.statement: The allowed alternative to annotate muted hits so the context packer can drop them exposes those hits to the agent before the drop, contradicting the user's mute boundary.
items.impact: Muted sensitive content can influence tool reasoning, logs, or later outputs despite the UI indicating it is excluded.
items.builder_discretion: Filter muted IDs before agent-visible result construction; keep exclusion metadata out-of-band and content-free.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Context Lens integration:** When Context Lens mutes messages, chatsearch MUST exclude muted message_ids from results returned to the agent (or annotate them as excluded so the context packer can drop them).

items.title: Project-scoped chat index lacks principal and lifecycle isolation
items.statement: A per-project index and pre-persistence secret scrubbing are specified, but not authorization by user/thread/role, deletion and edit propagation, re-scrubbing after policy changes, index rebuild, retention, or purge when a project is removed.
items.impact: Deleted, edited, unauthorized, or newly recognized sensitive messages can remain searchable within a shared project.
items.builder_discretion: Define principals, tombstones, update ordering, retention, rebuild, and verified purge semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Scope rule:** MUST be project-scoped (per-project Tantivy index directory).
- **Secrets policy:** Persisted chat index content MUST comply with PolicyRule:no_secrets_in_storage / INV-002 (mandatory strict secrets scrubbing before persistence).

items.title: Widened LSP operations lack executable request and result contracts
items.statement: The operations are only recommended names. This core does not define required inputs, output shapes, URI/project bounds, capability negotiation, stale-document handling, cancellation, timeout, unsupported-language behavior, or error codes.
items.impact: Callers and language-server adapters cannot implement or falsify interoperable behavior, especially for call hierarchy and workspace symbols.
items.builder_discretion: Specify per-operation schemas, capability/degraded states, freshness tokens, limits, cancellation, and canonical errors.

evidence.exact_quote: The `lsp` tool surface is widened beyond the minimal MVP read trio.
Recommended read operations:

items.title: Dynamic activity and warning UI has no accessibility, localization, or privacy contract
items.statement: Activity labels interpolate raw queries and URLs and prompt-injection state is represented as chips, but this core does not require accessible names, keyboard/screen-reader behavior, localization placeholders, bidirectional-text isolation, truncation, or sensitive-value redaction.
items.impact: Assistive-technology users may miss safety state, localized layouts can break, and sensitive queries or URLs can leak in activity surfaces.
items.builder_discretion: Define semantic roles/live-region behavior, localized templates, bidi isolation, redaction, and full-value reveal rules.

evidence.exact_quote: - Activity transparency uses `Reading Site: <url> (with browser interaction)` as a sub-annotation on the existing `Reading Site` label when browser interaction was needed for evidence access, not as a distinct seventh web activity label.

items.title: Glob negation example conflicts with separate exclusion ordering
items.statement: Path patterns are called glob-style and include a negated example, while exclusion is also a separate array applied after includes. The contract does not say whether leading ! is syntax, a literal, valid only in include_paths, or rejected.
items.impact: Adapters can crawl opposite URL sets for the same request and silently expose excluded content.
items.builder_discretion: Lock a grammar, escaping rules, case/percent-decoding normalization, and invalid-pattern errors with conformance vectors.

evidence.exact_quote: - `webcrawl` and `webmap` accept `include_paths?: string[]` and `exclude_paths?: string[]` as glob-style path matching, with examples such as `/docs/*`, `/api/**`, and `!/internal/*`; the patterns apply to the URL path component only, not the query string or fragment. Include rules are applied first to establish the candidate URL/path set, `/exclude_paths` removes matches from that set before crawl or map dispatch, and `search?: string` filters discovered URLs by search term.

items.title: Seed URLs are not reconciled with research read limits
items.statement: Up to five starting URLs are allowed, but the contract does not say whether they count toward max_sources, auto_read_cap, search iterations, citations, or the 120-second autonomous budget, nor which are dropped when limits conflict.
items.impact: The same inputs can exceed declared budgets or produce nondeterministic source selection.
items.builder_discretion: Define one ordered source budget and deterministic truncation/deduplication across seeds and discovered URLs.

evidence.exact_quote: - `webresearch` may also accept `starting_urls?: string[]` as optional seed URLs to begin research from, capped at five URLs; each URL follows the same normalization and validation rules as `webfetch`, and malformed or non-HTTP(S) URLs return `invalid_input`.

- Default execution limits begin with `websearch` `max_results = 8`; `webresearch` `max_sources = 6` and `auto_read_cap?: number`; the default auto-read cap = 4 pages before answering; `webextract` one URL only per invocation; `webcrawl` `max_pages = 25`, `max_depth = 2`, and `same_origin_only = true`; and `webmap` `max_pages = 50`, `max_depth = 3`, and `same_origin_only = true` unless a caller or provider capability contract supplies a narrower effective limit.

items.title: Lenient schema annotation can collide with user data
items.statement: Lenient mode injects `_schema_violation` into output without reserving that property, defining its location for arrays/scalars, or explaining behavior when the requested schema forbids additional properties or already defines the same key.
items.impact: The system can overwrite extracted user data or create output that violates the very schema consumers use for validation.
items.builder_discretion: Place violations in a separate envelope with JSON Pointer paths rather than mutating extracted_data.

evidence.exact_quote: - Schema validation modes apply to `webextract` and schema-backed `webresearch`. In `"strict"` mode, output MUST conform to schema, non-conforming fields are dropped, and missing required fields return `extraction_schema_mismatch`; in `"lenient"` mode (default), output uses best-effort conformance, keeps non-conforming fields with `_schema_violation: true` annotation, and treats missing required fields as a warning, not an error.

items.title: Removed pages are indistinguishable from partial crawl failure
items.statement: A page absent from the current crawl becomes removed, but no rule distinguishes true removal from robots denial, timeout, authentication loss, provider truncation, network loss, or an effective depth/page limit.
items.impact: Consumers can delete or alert on content that was merely unreachable, and GUI change summaries can make a false claim.
items.builder_discretion: Require complete baseline coverage before removed and otherwise emit unknown/unobserved with cause and coverage delta.

items.impact: Transient loss can cause duplicate work, abandoned sessions, or misleading terminal failure with no actionable recovery path.
items.builder_discretion: Define retryability and resume tokens per operation, with idempotency and session-cleanup rules.

dimension_assessments.summary: Web callers are enumerated, but LSP operation consumers and deterministic routing obligations remain under-specified.
Unsupported-input outcomes, partial format success, action timeout state, and crawl change state lack one coherent transition model.
Concurrent and interrupted crawl generations can race on the undefined previous-crawl baseline.
Action arrays, requested formats, and crawl coverage lack explicit partial-completion semantics.
Neither browser action batches nor multi-file LSP rename define rollback, safe retry, or resume behavior.
Wildcard discovery, redirect/address enforcement, iframe origins, and chat-index principals leave authority gaps.
Default cache persistence and chat indexing lack complete partition, retention, mutation, and purge contracts.
URL resolution, page prompt injection, hostile binary responses, schema expansion, and annotation collision remain exploitable negative space.
Single success state can hide missing artifacts, and change tracking can falsely label unreachable pages removed.
Reason codes exist, but retries, backoff, checkpointing, offline cache behavior, and safe provider fallback are not defined.
Schema complexity, iframe fan-out, and composition of seed/read limits are not bounded sufficiently.
Page accessibility structure is explicit, but activity and safety-chip presentation lacks assistive-technology requirements.
Interpolated query/URL activity labels have no localization, bidi, truncation, or redaction contract.
Action vocabularies and glob negation can normalize incompatibly across adapters and legacy callers.
The common result envelope, payload refs, fallback fields, source provenance, and degraded reason codes provide strong observability coverage.
LSP rename is approval-gated but lacks transactional apply, validation, and rollback requirements.
